text:
ashwin: quick check — i ran the predictive-headroom job against last 30 days and the smoothing window we had is underprovisioning EU-west during business hours. noticed repeated short spikes that blow past burst headroom :thinking_face:

maria: hmm can you share the query + windows? is this with the 5m lookback or the new 2h forecast horizon?

ashwin: 5m for the infra alert, 2h for the predictive headroom. gist: it predicts average + 2 sigma, but the short spikes are ~3-4 sigma and last 30-90s (so batching doesnt help)

kai: those transient 90s spikes are the tricky ones — they bypass continuous batching and force new allocations. we saw same pattern last month after the marketing push. cost hit was ~8% on GPU hours in eu-west for the day.

jamie: could we try a tiny prewarm buffer instead of full burst allocation? say reserve 10% steady plus a tiny 30s prewarm pool that sits cold? keeps steady economics but reduces ops start-up latency.

ashwin: prototype config i tested: ```yaml
autoscale:
  steady_pct: 0.10
  predictive_horizon: 2h
  spike_guard:
    window_s: 90
    prewarm_pct: 0.03
    hard_burst_limit_gpu: 8
```
that prewarm_pct at 3% shaved tail p95 latency while only adding ~1.2% GPU hours overall.

maria: nice. did you factor regional egress constraints? prewarm nodes still need model weights pulled and that saturates network in us-east-1 during prime time. we should gate prewarm by dataplane egress budget.

kai: +1, also ensure prewarm uses quantized variant if available (weights are smaller). we can route prewarm to a quantized pool via policy: `model_variant: q4_0`

jamie: what about safety guardrails — if prewarm fails or egress quota is exceeded, fall back to delayed burst instead of failing requests. something like: `fallback: delayed-burst` and a max-queue-time 2s.

ashwin: agree. i also added a cost cutoff so we dont allow prewarm to spin if day budget > 95% commit. in code: ```json
{"budget_check": "day_commit_pct < 0.95"}
```

oncall-bot: notice: scheduled model sync in eu-west at 03:00 UTC may bump network usage by ~120MB/sec for 5m window.

maria: good catch — we should disable prewarm during that sync window or drop prewarm_pct to 0.

kai: next steps: ashwin to run A/B for 3 days with prewarm_pct=0.03 + quantized prewarm, jamie to add fallback policy, maria to add egress gating rule. i'll own the analysis dashboard. sound good? :thumbsup:

jamie: sounds good — i'll open a short PR for fallback policy and add tests for max-queue-time.

ashwin: kicking off the A/B now. will post results in this thread in 72h with cost + p95 latency deltas.

maria: thanks — tagging infra-review for FYI. @kai @jamie keep me posted if any region shows weird debt.

kai: noted, will watch telemetry and set a temp alert for prewarm network saturation.

ashwin: thanks everyone. low-risk experiment but could buy us much of the tail improvement without large reserved commits.
